title: Los Altos 1031 Exchange Coordination
name: Los Altos 1031 Exchange Coordination
metaTitle: Los Altos 1031 Exchange Coordination | San Jose, CA
metaDescription: 1031 exchange coordination for Los Altos State Street retail, medical and professional office, and long-held low-basis parcels near Foothill Expressway.

sections.html: Los Altos runs a small, tightly held commercial market centered on State Street, with medical and professional office space filling out the rest of the inventory near Foothill Expressway. Ownership here tends to be long-tenured and Prop 13-protected, so a Los Altos listing usually represents a rare event rather than routine turnover. An exchanger targeting this town should expect to move quickly once a suitable property surfaces, since a second comparable option rarely appears before the 45-day identification window closes. The town's proximity to Google, Meta, and other Peninsula and South Bay employers supports the high household income that keeps State Street rents elevated, even though very little of that broader tech employment actually sits within Los Altos city limits itself.

sections.heading: Small-Format Retail and Restaurant Space Along State Street
sections.html: State Street carries most of downtown Los Altos's retail and restaurant space, and the buildings are older two- and one-story structures with limited square footage per storefront. Rents track the town's high-income resident base rather than typical suburban retail metrics, and vacancy has historically stayed low because so few landlords choose to sell. A buyer identifying a State Street property as replacement property should confirm actual trailing sales figures from the tenant where possible, since restaurant and specialty retail leases in this corridor are often percentage-rent structured on top of a modest base. Parking along State Street itself is limited, and several tenants lean on nearby public lots rather than dedicated spaces, so a buyer should confirm the actual parking arrangement tied to the specific storefront rather than assuming on-site parking exists.

sections.heading: Medical and Professional Office Serving a High-Net-Worth Client Base
sections.html: Small medical and professional office buildings near Foothill Expressway and around the downtown core serve a client base that skews toward specialty medical practices, wealth management, and legal services catering to the surrounding residential wealth. These buildings tend to run smaller floor plates than office product in San Jose or Sunnyvale, and tenant improvement allowances reflect that boutique scale rather than large corporate build-outs. A replacement property buyer should review the tenant mix for concentration risk, since a single-practice building depends heavily on that one tenant's lease renewal.

sections.heading: Land Scarcity and Long-Held Basis Among Local Owners
sections.html:
Los Altos has almost no vacant commercially zoned land left, and most owners have held their buildings long enough that a sale without an exchange would trigger a substantial gain. A diligence file for Los Altos replacement property typically includes:

  • Current rent roll with lease term and renewal options
  • Percentage-rent or specialty-retail lease structure detail
  • Tenant concentration analysis for single-practice office buildings
  • Prop 13 basis history from the county assessor
  • Parking ratio confirmation against current zoning
  • Phase I environmental site assessment

Because so little new supply can be built, a buyer's leverage in negotiating price concessions on a Los Altos property is generally limited compared with markets where new construction competes for tenants.

sections.heading: Identification Windows When Inventory Turns Over Rarely
sections.html: Given how infrequently Los Altos commercial property comes to market, many exchangers use the 200% rule to identify a broader set of candidates, including comparable small-format retail or medical office in adjacent Santa Clara County towns, rather than betting the entire exchange on one Los Altos address. The identification letter should still describe each backup candidate with the same specificity as the frontrunner, listing the address and a reasonable description of the property rather than a general category.

sections.heading: Coordinating the Exchange With Lenders Unfamiliar With Thin Markets
sections.html: Lenders who do not regularly underwrite Los Altos properties sometimes struggle to find comparable sales for an appraisal, given how few transactions occur, and a buyer should flag this early so the lender can commission an appraiser with local experience rather than defaulting to broader Santa Clara County comps. The qualified intermediary should stay in direct contact with escrow throughout to keep the closing timeline aligned with the 180-day exchange period; this description covers process only, and a tax advisor should confirm gain and basis treatment before the exchange agreement is signed.

faqs.q: Why is Los Altos commercial inventory so hard to find?
faqs.a: Ownership along State Street and near Foothill Expressway tends to be long-held and Prop 13-protected, so listings are rare events rather than routine turnover, and a Los Altos exchange candidate often has no direct comparable available at the same time.

faqs.q: What should I check on a State Street restaurant or retail lease?
faqs.a: Confirm whether the lease is structured with percentage rent on top of a base, which is common for specialty retail and restaurant tenants here, and review trailing sales figures where the tenant is willing to share them.

faqs.q: Is single-tenant concentration a risk in Los Altos medical office buildings?
faqs.a: Yes. Many of these buildings run smaller floor plates centered on one or two specialty practices, so losing that tenant at renewal has an outsized effect on income compared with a multi-tenant building.

faqs.q: Should I identify properties outside Los Altos as backup candidates?
faqs.a: Many exchangers do, using the 200% rule to name comparable small-format retail or medical office in nearby towns, since Los Altos itself may not produce a second viable option before the 45-day deadline.

faqs.q: Why might a lender need extra time to appraise a Los Altos property?
faqs.a: Because so few transactions occur, an appraiser may need to look beyond the immediate area for comparable sales, and flagging this early helps keep the underwriting timeline aligned with the exchange deadlines.
